viNames.name: Tép Blue Dream (bán dưới tên tiếng Anh Blue Velvet Shrimp)
Tép màu xanh (nhóm Tép Màu Neocaridina)

origin.fact: It is a colour form of Neocaridina davidi, the same wild species that gave the red cherry shrimp, and it came from Taiwan. The source gives no date or named breeder.
One source says Blue Velvets were bred from blue carbon rili stock, while Blue Dreams came from chocolate Neocaridina.
Flip Aquatics says the blue colour came from Red Rili Neocaridina.
Aquatic Arts says it was bred from the same wild type as Sakura red cherry shrimp, but that how it was developed is poorly documented.
One source says the blue colour was first selectively bred in Taiwan.

looks.fact: Bright blue body. Females are larger and a deeper blue than males, which are smaller and paler.
Higher grades have more intense colour. Nearly see-through shrimp are the lowest grade. A better grade does not mean a healthier shrimp.
The blue covers most of the body. Its strength varies by individual, sex and lighting, so judge a whole colony or a video, not one photo.
The blue looks brightest under low light on a dark substrate.

lines.fact: Blue Dream is meant to be a more solid blue, but it can look almost the same as Blue Velvet. Similar blues include blue pearl, blue jelly, blue tiger and blue rili.
Aquatic Arts sells a darker 'Dream Blue Velvet' and a lighter 'Sky Blue Velvet'.
A Vietnamese shop treats Blue Dream and Blue Velvet as one product, a medium-to-deep blue morph.

keeping.fact: The tank should hold at least about 19 L (5 US gal), and beginners do better with more. It must be fully cycled with zero ammonia and nitrite and low nitrate.
KH 3–15 and TDS 150–250. A heater is usually not needed unless the temperature swings.
Copper is toxic to them, whether it comes from medicines, fertilisers or copper sulfate in food. Overfeeding is a common cause of death, and established tanks with biofilm may need little extra food.
Safe tankmates: other dwarf shrimp, Corydoras, Otocinclus, guppies, small tetras and snails. Avoid angelfish, bettas, cichlids, gouramis, goldfish, large catfish and crayfish.
Peaceful and leaves plants alone, so it suits moss tanks, nano tanks and shrimp-only tanks. Keep it apart from Caridina shrimp, which need different water.

breeding.fact: Breeds easily. Females carry 30–50 eggs, and the young hatch as tiny adults with no larval stage. They mature in about 3 months.
Eggs hatch in about 30 days. Fry can stay in the main tank if the filter intake has a sponge.
Mixing it with other Neocaridina colours can produce brown, wild-type offspring. Selective breeding improves the colour over generations.
Keep only one colour line per tank to hold the blue steady. Mixed lines give unpredictable young.

health.fact: Hardy overall, but sensitive to ammonia and nitrite, so it needs stable water.
Copper in any form is toxic to it.
Do not keep changing water parameters to try to force a deeper blue.

buying.fact: Several blue Neocaridina look alike and are often mislabelled in local stores. Buy from a specialist shrimp seller or an experienced hobbyist.
Young shrimp may colour up more once settled, so pale juveniles are not always low grade.
Judge colour from the real colony or a video, not one photo. A Vietnamese shop gives a reference price of about 20,000 VND per shrimp.

controversy.fact: Feral Neocaridina davidi from the aquarium trade have set up populations in warm, thermally polluted waters in Germany, Hungary and Slovakia. Researchers expect further spread and found a microsporidian parasite in feral populations.

Plichta et al. (2021) call the ornamental N. davidi a potentially invasive species and found that colour morphs differ in which backgrounds they prefer. This may affect how likely each morph is to establish in the wild.
